whatYouGet: A full SwiftUI color/type token set matching Duolingo's saturated gamification palette and the Feather Bold + DIN Rounded type ladder
The signature 3D 'ledge' button and skill-node components, including press-collapse physics and haptic/sound pairing rules
A celebration-takeover and curved learning-path component spec, ready to adapt to any streak-driven or lesson-based product
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in gamified consumer apps — the kind of designer who has shipped habit-loop mechanics (streaks, XP, lives) and knows how to make a 3D-feeling button that collapses convincingly on press. You think in terms of tactile feedback loops: color + haptic + sound + motion, never just one channel.

<reference_data>
Color roles (light mode primary):
- Feather Green #58CC02 (primary CTA / correct answer / completed node fill) — the verb color
- Button Green Shadow #58A700 (the ledge beneath every green button, offset 0 4px 0)
- Mask Green #89E219 (progress bar top highlight, pulse rings)
- Cardinal Red #FF4B4B / ledge #E53030 (wrong answer, lost heart, destructive only)
- Fox Orange #FF9600 (streak flame), Bee Yellow #FFC800 (gems/rewards), Macaw Blue #1CB0F6 (info/tips), Beetle Purple #CE82FF (premium accent)
- Canvas: Snow #FFFFFF light / Dark Canvas #131F24 (blue-black, never true black) dark
- Surfaces: Polar #F7F7F7, Swan #E5E5E5 (+ ledge #C4C4C4)
- Text: Eel #4B4B4B (primary), Hare #AFAFAF (secondary), Wolf #777777 (tertiary)

Type ladder (two families only):
- Feather Bold (proprietary display/numbers face; fall back to SF Pro Rounded) at 56pt/700 hero numbers, 34pt/700 wordmark, 28pt/700 screen titles, 22pt/700 question prompts, 18pt/700 HUD numbers
- DIN Next Rounded Pro (UI workhorse; fall back to SF Pro Rounded) at 20pt/800 section headers, 17pt/800 UPPERCASE button labels (tracked +0.4pt), 16pt/400 body, 14pt/500 helper text, 11pt/700 tab labels
- Weight is concentrated at 400/500/700/800 only — no thin or light weights anywhere

Spacing/radius/shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt; scale 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48/56/72/96
- Corner radii: 12pt tiles, 16pt cards/primary buttons, 20pt section-hero cards, 500pt full pills, 50% circular nodes
- Depth model is NOT shadow — it's a solid-color 'ledge': a 4pt-tall darker-tone slab directly beneath every interactive surface (2pt for tiles/chips, 4pt for buttons/nodes), with zero blur

Named distinctive patterns:
1. The 3D Ledge Button — top face + darker offset ledge that visually disappears when the face translates down on press
2. The curved Learning Path — vertically scrolling trail of 80pt circular skill nodes offset in an alternating ±60pt wave, connected by an 8pt dashed line, current node pulsing to 96pt
3. HUD chips (streak flame/gems/hearts) as 32pt pill readouts with icon + Feather Bold number
4. Full-screen celebration takeover on lesson complete — green background, mascot illustration, confetti burst, XP counter
5. Answer tiles that shift fill/border color to signal correct/wrong, paired with a shake or bounce animation
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Every primary interactive element (buttons, skill nodes) gets the ledge treatment — never substitute a drop shadow, since the ledge collapsing on press IS the tactile signature.
2. Reserve the primary green strictly for the main action and the correct-answer state; never use it decoratively elsewhere.
3. Pair every correct/wrong feedback moment with a color change AND a haptic AND a sound AND a motion — dropping any one channel breaks the 'game feel' this system depends on.
4. Keep button labels short, uppercase, and DIN Rounded weight 800 with +0.4pt tracking — never a full sentence on a CTA.
5. Round every interactive surface — no sharp corners on tappable elements; circles for nodes/avatars, pills for chips/progress, 12–16pt on cards and tiles.
6. Treat numbers (streaks, XP, gem counts) as celebratory: set them roughly 2x the size of surrounding UI text in the display face, never the body face.
7. Never rely on red/green alone for correctness signaling — always pair the color with an icon (checkmark/x) so the pattern stays colorblind-safe.
8. Keep the emotional-anchor mascot (or equivalent brand character) large and unsubtle whenever it appears — celebration and empty-state illustrations should dominate, never sit as a small corner decoration.
9. Curve or wave any primary linear-progress navigation rather than rendering it as a straight vertical list — the wave silhouette is what reads as recognizable at a glance.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line concept:
- Primary habit/action being gamified (e.g., daily lesson, workout, savings streak):
- Core reward currency (XP, points, gems, streak days — name it):
- Mascot or brand character (name + personality, if any):
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version, iPhone/iPad support):
- Light/dark mode requirement:
- Primary CTA verb (e.g., "Continue", "Start", "Check"):
- Any existing brand colors that must be respected alongside or instead of the reference greens/reds:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` extension file implementing the full token set above, adapted to the project's brand colors where specified.
2. A reusable `LedgeButton` component (SwiftUI) implementing the 3D ledge press/release animation with configurable top/ledge colors and haptic hook.
3. A skill-node or progress-node component with locked/current/completed states and the pulsing 'current' ring animation.
4. A curved path/track layout component generating the alternating-offset wave for a vertical scroll of nodes.
5. A full-screen celebration takeover view (confetti layer + mascot/hero art slot + reward counter) with motion timing specified in milliseconds.
6. A HUD chip row component for the primary reward currencies (streak/points/lives equivalents).
7. A short accessibility note covering Reduce Motion fallback, VoiceOver labels for state-bearing components, and colorblind-safe correctness signaling.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer specializing in conversational AI interfaces, with deep experience making a chat surface read like a calm reading document rather than a busy message feed. You understand how to ration a single brand gradient so it signals 'intelligence happening' without ever becoming decorative noise.

<reference_data>
Color roles:
- Brand gradient: linear sweep #4285F4 (0%) → #9B72CB (50%) → #D96570 (100%) — reserved for the sparkle mark, streaming-edge shimmer, prompt-bar focus ring, and featured-chip hairlines only; never a body-text tint or button fill
- Interactive primary: solid Google Blue #4285F4 (dark-mode variant #8AB4F8) for the active send button and links; pressed state #3367D6
- Canvas: Canvas White #FFFFFF light / Dark Canvas #1E1E1E dark — no cards, no boxes
- Surface Soft #F0F4F9 light / #282A2C dark — user-turn chip, prompt bar, suggestion chips, drawer
- Text: Primary #1F1F1F light / #E3E3E3 dark; Secondary #5F6368 light / #9AA0A6 dark
- Semantic: Success #1E8E3E/#81C995, Warning #F9AB00, Error #D93025/#F28B82

Type ladder (Google Sans + Inter fallback):
- Greeting/hero 28pt/500 tracked -0.2pt ("Hello, [name]")
- Screen title 22pt/500, section header 18pt/500
- Answer body 16pt/400 at 1.55 line-height — the reading-optimized core content size
- User-turn text 16pt/400 at 1.45 line-height
- Suggestion chip label 14pt/500, metadata 13pt/400
- Code blocks in Roboto Mono 14pt/400 at 1.5 line-height
- Weights concentrated at 400/500/700 only, negative tracking reserved for the greeting/titles alone

Spacing/radius/shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt; turn spacing 24pt between a user turn and reply, 32pt between full exchanges
- Radii: 12pt code blocks, 18pt suggestion chips, 20pt user-turn chip (4pt on the bottom-trailing 'pointing' corner), 26pt prompt bar, 500pt pills, 50% circles
- Almost shadowless: conversation content is flat (Level 0); only the prompt bar gets a whisper shadow (~0 1px 4px), and the gradient focus ring IS the elevation cue, not a shadow

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Document-not-feed canvas — no chat bubbles around the assistant reply, plain markdown text directly on canvas
2. Gradient sparkle ✦ mark — leads every assistant turn and the empty-state hero, the single brand signifier
3. Streaming shimmer — a soft ~120pt-wide gradient highlight sweeps the leading edge of newly generated text, with a 3-dot gradient 'thinking' pulse before the first token
4. Gradient focus ring on the prompt bar — a 1.5pt gradient stroke wrapping the composer only while it's focused, standing in for a glow
5. Trailing-aligned gray user chip with an asymmetric 4pt 'pointing' corner, max ~80% width, no avatar or name
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never wrap the assistant's reply in a bubble or card — it must render as plain flowing text directly on the canvas, full conversation-column width.
2. Ration the brand gradient to exactly four places: the sparkle mark, the streaming-edge shimmer, the prompt-bar focus ring, and featured suggestion-chip hairlines — never as a fill behind paragraphs or inside a button background.
3. Keep the interactive primary (send button, links) as solid brand blue, distinct from the gradient — the gradient signals thinking, blue signals 'tap me'.
4. Set answer body copy at 16pt with 1.55 line-height minimum; this is a reading surface, so never compress line-height to save vertical space.
5. Never add a bottom tab bar — navigation is a single side drawer; if the product needs more sections, add them inside the drawer, not as tabs.
6. Keep the gradient stops identical across light and dark mode — the brand color is the one thing that must never adapt to theme.
7. Always show a thinking indicator before the first streamed token arrives, and always fade the streaming cursor/shimmer out (not snap off) when generation completes.
8. Keep the conversation shadowless; the only surfaces allowed real elevation are the floating prompt bar and true overlays (drawer, sheets, model picker).
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line concept:
- What the assistant is for (general chat, coding help, research, etc.):
- Brand gradient or accent colors to substitute for the reference gradient (if different from Gemini's):
- Model/mode names to show in the model-selector control:
- Multimodal input needed (image, file, camera attach)?
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version, iPad support):
- Light/dark mode requirement:
- Any existing typeface constraints:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color`, `Font`, and `LinearGradient` token extension implementing the full palette and type ladder, parameterized to the project's brand gradient.
2. A conversation view composing the trailing-aligned user chip and the plain-text assistant turn with the leading gradient sparkle.
3. A streaming-response component: token-by-token text reveal, the gradient leading-edge shimmer overlay, and the 3-dot thinking indicator.
4. A gradient-ring prompt-bar component with the '+' attach control, placeholder state, and the send-button-to-stop-button morph.
5. A suggestion-chip row component for the empty state, including the featured-chip gradient hairline variant.
6. A side-drawer navigation component (grouped by day, e.g. "Today"/"Previous 7 Days") replacing any tab-bar assumption.
7. A short accessibility note covering Reduce Motion fallback for the shimmer/sparkle, and Dynamic Type behavior for greeting/body vs. fixed-size prompt-bar chrome.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in dense, information-first developer tools. You think in terms of Primer-style semantic color discipline: every hue in the interface means one specific thing to an engineer reading it at a glance, and you never spend a color decoratively.

<reference_data>
Color roles (dark default — canvas is a first-class peer in light):
- Canvas Default #0D1117 (blue-tinted near-black, never pure black), stepped surfaces Canvas Subtle #161B22 and Canvas Inset #21262D, Border Default #30363D
- Accent FG #2F81F7 dark / #0969DA light — links, owner/name, active/selected states ONLY, never body text
- Button Primary #238636 dark / #1F883D light — RESERVED exclusively for the 'Code' download button and 'Merge pull request'; never a generic CTA
- Semantic state (fixed, never swapped): Open/success #3FB950, Merged #A371F7 (purple = done), Closed/danger #F85149, Draft/neutral #6E7681, Attention #D29922
- FG Default #E6EDF3 dark / #1F2328 light (primary text), FG Muted #7D8590 dark / #656D76 light (secondary/metadata)
- Contributions heatmap 5-step ramp (exact, never recolor): L0 #161B22 → L1 #0E4429 → L2 #006D32 → L3 #26A641 → L4 #39D353 (light-mode equivalents #EBEDF0→#9BE9A8→#40C463→#30A14E→#216E39)
- Tab-strip active underline: orange-coral #F78166

Type ladder (Mona Sans UI + monospace for code):
- Repo title 24pt/700 tracked -0.3pt, section 20pt/600, subtitle 16pt/600
- Body 14pt/400, body-strong 14pt/600 (file names)
- Monospace (SF Mono / JetBrains Mono fallback) at 13pt/400 for code/blob/diffs, 12pt/600 for SHA/branch chips — monospace is mandatory here, never sans
- Weight ladder is 400/600/700/800 concentrated; numbers/counts use tabular figures so columns align

Spacing/radius/shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt; list-row vertical padding 9-12pt (deliberately dense); screen horizontal inset 16pt
- Radii: 4pt badges/heatmap squares, 6pt buttons/inputs/branch pill, 8pt cards (file list, README), 12pt sheets, 999pt state pills/labels, 50% avatars
- Depth model is stepped surface luminance + 1pt borders, NOT drop-shadows; only true overlays (dropdowns, sheets) get a shadow, and it's a deep near-black blue-tinted shadow

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Repo header composition: owner/name (both accent blue, name bold) → description → language-dot/star/fork stats row
2. Tab strip (Code · Issues · Pull requests · Actions) with a 2pt orange-coral underline on the active item, count badges as small pills
3. Contributions heatmap — a grid of squares in the fixed 5-step ramp with a Less→More legend and tap-for-tooltip
4. State pills and color-tinted issue labels (label's own hex at 10% fill / 40% border / full-hex text)
5. Diff viewer with green/red line-background washes, a muted right-aligned line-number gutter, and code that scrolls horizontally rather than wraps
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Treat the reserved green as sacred — it may only ever label a 'download code' or 'merge' action; every other primary action uses the default (neutral) button style.
2. Keep state colors fixed and never swap their meaning: open is always green, merged is always purple, closed is always red, draft is always grey — a developer reads these as facts, not styling choices.
3. Render ALL code, commit SHAs, file paths, and branch names in a monospace face — alignment and glyph distinction (0 vs O, l vs 1) are functional requirements, not stylistic ones.
4. Define card and list-region boundaries with a 1pt border plus a luminance step, never a drop-shadow — shadows are reserved for true floating overlays only.
5. Never recolor or reorder the contributions-heatmap ramp; it is the single most recognizable visual in this system and its meaning depends on staying exact.
6. Keep code lines un-wrapped — long lines scroll horizontally inside their own container, never reflow.
7. Reserve accent blue strictly for links, active states, and the owner/name identity string — never let it appear in body copy.
8. Favor density over whitespace throughout: this is a professional tool, so tight row padding (9-12pt) and clear bordered regions communicate more information per screen than generous breathing room would.
9. Give every color-tinted label (bug/enhancement/etc.) the same formula — text in the label's own hue, border at 40% alpha, fill at 10% alpha — so custom label colors never need a bespoke rule.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line concept:
- What kind of 'repository' or project entity this app centers on (if not literal git repos):
- Which semantic states need color-coding (e.g., open/merged/closed, or your own status set):
- Whether a contributions-style activity heatmap applies to this product, and what activity it should track:
- Whether a diff/comparison view is needed:
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version, iPad multi-pane support):
- Light/dark mode requirement (dark-default, per this system):
- Any existing brand colors that must coexist with the reserved green/blue:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension implementing the full Primer-style palette (dark-default with light peer) and the Mona Sans + monospace type ladder.
2. A repo/project header component: title row, description, and a stats row with a colored dot + counts.
3. A tab-strip component with the sliding orange-coral active underline and count badges.
4. A contributions-heatmap grid component using the exact 5-step ramp, with a tap-for-tooltip interaction.
5. State-pill and color-tinted label-chip components implementing the fixed semantic mapping and the label-color-derived tint formula.
6. A diff-viewer layout: line-background washes, gutter, and file-header with addition/deletion counts.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in high-volume list-based messaging apps. You have deep experience with Material Design's layered elevation model on iOS and know how to keep an inbox calm and scannable by rationing color to exactly one structural accent.

<reference_data>
Color roles:
- Canvas Light #FFFFFF (pure, unbranded — content carries the color, not chrome) / Dark Canvas #202124 (near-black charcoal, never true #000)
- Gmail Red #D93025 — reserved almost exclusively for the Compose FAB and destructive actions ("Delete forever"); pressed #B3261E
- Google 4-color brand set applied ONLY to avatars/chips/labels, never structural UI: Red #EA4335, Yellow #FBBC04, Green #34A853, Blue #4285F4
- Text Link #1A73E8 (deeper than Google Blue) — used for hyperlinks and, uniquely, as button text color on tonal buttons
- Text Primary #202124 / dark #E8EAED; Text Secondary #5F6368 / dark #BDC1C6
- Divider #DADCE0 / dark #3C4043; Surface Light #F6F8FC / dark #28292C
- Semantic: Starred Yellow #F5BA18 (not gold #FFD700), Archive teal-green #1E8E3E, Snooze purple #A142F4, Selected-row #E8F0FE

Type ladder (two families, strict division):
- Google Sans carries emotion/structure: screen titles 28pt/400, section headers 13pt/500 tracked 0.8pt uppercase ("TODAY"), buttons/labels/tabs 12-17pt/500
- Roboto carries information: email snippets 13pt/400, thread body 15pt/400, timestamps 13pt/400 — read state also flips sender/subject from Google Sans 500 (unread/bold) to Roboto 400 (read)
- Weight is the primary unread signal (bold sender + bold subject), never color alone
- Never mix the two families within a single text block

Spacing/radius/shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt; fixed 72pt-tall email rows with 16pt horizontal insets
- Radii: 16pt Compose-FAB squircle (Material You signature, NOT a circle), 500pt pills (buttons, tab active-indicator, label chips), 50% avatars, 8pt small chip squircles
- Elevation is layered Material-style (a crisp close shadow + a softer distant shadow per level) — inbox rows themselves are flat/shadowless, separation is whitespace only

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Compose FAB — a 56×56pt red 16pt-radius squircle bottom-right with a white pencil glyph; shrinks to icon-only on scroll-down, re-expands (and grows a "Compose" label on wide/tablet widths) on scroll-up
2. Swipeable email row — left-swipe reveals a teal archive pane, right-swipe reveals a red delete pane, both user-configurable
3. Unread signaling via weight change (bold sender + subject), not color, with an optional thin colored 'important' stripe
4. Smart Reply chips — 3 auto-generated pill suggestions in link-blue outline style, horizontally scrolling above the keyboard in thread view
5. Material-You active-tab indicator — a soft tinted pill (not a full-tab background) sitting behind the active tab-bar icon
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Keep the canvas unbranded — pure white (or near-black dark), with the Gmail red confined to the Compose FAB and destructive actions only; never color the surrounding chrome.
2. Make the Compose FAB a 16pt-radius squircle, never a circle — that shape distinction is part of the Material You brand signature.
3. Signal unread state through weight (bold sender + subject), not color alone — color-only unread cues get lost against a busy inbox.
4. Never mix the titles/structure typeface with the body/information typeface inside the same text block — pick one per block based on its role.
5. Apply any secondary brand colors (a 4-color set or similar) only to avatars, category chips, and suggestion chips — never to structural UI elements like nav bars or dividers.
6. Keep list rows completely flat (no shadow); only floating elements — the FAB, sheets, dialogs — earn Material's layered close+distant shadow treatment.
7. Always implement left-swipe and right-swipe as distinct, user-configurable actions on list rows, with a colored reveal pane and a completion threshold around 40% of the swipe width.
8. Never let the Compose FAB fully disappear — on scroll it may shrink to icon-only, but it must always remain visible and reachable.
9. Keep starred/marked states in the exact defined hue (not a generic 'gold') so the app's visual vocabulary stays consistent across screens.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line concept:
- What kind of list this inbox represents (email, messages, tasks, notifications):
- Primary compose/create action and its icon:
- Swipe actions needed (archive/delete/snooze/mark-read, or custom):
- Any auto-suggestion or smart-reply-style feature to include:
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version, iPad split-view support):
- Light/dark mode requirement:
- Existing brand accent color to substitute for Gmail red, if different:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension implementing the full palette and the two-typeface type ladder with weight-based read/unread logic.
2. A Compose-FAB component: squircle shape, scroll-collapse/expand behavior, and the pressed/haptic states.
3. A swipeable list-row component with configurable left/right actions, reveal panes, and threshold-commit gesture logic.
4. A layered Material-style shadow/elevation token set (crisp + soft shadow pairs per level) and where each level applies.
5. A Smart-Reply-style chip row component (outline pill, link-color text, horizontal scroll).
6. A bottom tab bar component with the Material-You tinted-pill active indicator.
7. A short accessibility note on Dynamic Type scaling (what scales vs. stays fixed) and VoiceOver labeling for unread/starred/swipe-action state.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in editorial, content-first catalog apps. You understand how to let photographic cover art be the sole source of color saturation in an interface while everything else — chrome, type, structure — stays warm, quiet, and restrained.

<reference_data>
Color roles:
- Tan Paper #F4F1EA (signature light canvas — warm, paper-like, never pure white) / Dark Canvas #161310 (warm ink-brown, never true black)
- Goodreads Brown #382110 — primary brand surface (shelf headers, logomark, secondary button); shifts to tan-gold #C9883D for active states on dark (brown reads muddy on dark)
- Rating Amber #E9A100 — the single load-bearing accent, identical light and dark, reserved almost exclusively for the five-star rating; empty star rail #D8D2C4 light / #4A3F2C dark
- Shelf Green #409D69 — the one other CTA color, used only for the primary 'add to shelf' action; pressed #348355
- Link Teal #00635D light / #6FB3AD dark — author names and hyperlinks, deliberately never blue
- Text Primary #382110 light / #EDE6D8 dark (warm brown-black, not pure black); Text Secondary #6B5E47 / #B3A88F

Type ladder (serif reads, sans operates):
- Merriweather (reading serif) for anything the user reads: screen title 30pt/900, book title 23pt/900 tracked -0.2pt, section header 19pt/700, body/review/synopsis 15pt/400 at 1.6 line-height
- Lato (UI sans) for anything the user acts on: buttons 17pt/900, author/bold labels 14pt/700, metadata 13pt/400, overline 11pt/700 tracked 0.6pt uppercase
- Numerals (ratings counts, page counts, percentages) always render in the sans face for tabular clarity, even inside serif-heavy blocks

- Radii: nearly-square 3pt book covers (like real books), 4pt buttons/segmented controls, 6-8pt cards/search fields, 12pt sheets, 999pt shelf-status pills
- Shadow is used sparingly and warmly — the book cover is the ONE element that always gets a real, warm-tinted (brown-black, not neutral grey) drop shadow because physical books cast shadows; UI cards get only a faint lift, the canvas itself stays flat

Named distinctive patterns:

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in dark-only, terminal-inspired conversational interfaces. You favor radical monochrome restraint and know how to make a single reserved accent color do all of an interface's chromatic signaling.

<reference_data>
Color roles (dark-only, no light mode shipped):
- Canvas Black #000000 — true OLED black, never softened to #121212 or similar
- Accent White #FFFFFF (pressed #D7DBDC) — the functional 'accent': active mode-pill fill, enabled send button, streaming cursor
- Surface 1 #16181C (user bubble, prompt-bar field), Surface 2 #1E2126 (citation cards, sheets), Surface 3 #272A2E (pressed/active states)
- Divider #2F3336 — hairlines, citation-card borders, prompt-bar border
- Text Primary #E7E9EA (intentionally not pure white, for reading comfort), Text Secondary #71767B, Text Tertiary #4D5156
- Link Blue #1D9BF0 — the ONLY chromatic color in the entire UI, reserved for links and post-citation taps; pressed #1A8CD8
- Semantic: Success Green #00BA7C (copy-confirmed toast only), Error Red #F4212E, rare Warning Amber #FFD400

Type ladder (Inter, slashed-zero on):
- Screen title 28pt/700 tracked -0.4pt, section header 20pt/700
- Assistant body 16pt/400 at 1.55 line-height (the reading surface), user message 16pt/400 at 1.45
- Mode-pill label 14pt/600, citation author 14pt/700, citation handle/meta 13pt/400
- Code in SF Mono 13.5pt/400 with slashed-zero numerals enabled via font-feature 'zero' 1
- Weight band strictly 400/600/700 — no light or black weights

Spacing/radius/shadow:
- Base spacing unit 4pt; turn spacing 24pt user-to-reply, 32pt between full turns
- Radii: 4pt inline code, 14-16pt suggestion chips/citation cards/code blocks, 20pt user bubble (with a 6pt 'tail' corner), 24pt prompt bar, 18pt/full mode-toggle pill, 50% circles
- Almost no shadow anywhere in-conversation — elevation comes from surface VALUE steps (#000000 → #16181C → #1E2126) plus 1pt borders; shadow appears only on true floating overlays (sheets, history slide-over) as a deep near-black blur

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Literal teletype streaming reveal — tokens appear left-to-right with NO bouncy per-character animation, trailed by a blinking block cursor (▍) at ~530ms on/off
2. X post citation card (signature surface) — avatar, name, verified check, handle/timestamp, 4-line-clamp post body, engagement footer, entire card tappable
3. Assistant reply as plain full-width text with zero bubble — only the user message and citation cards get a surface at all
4. Mode-toggle segmented pill (e.g. Regular/Fun) as the primary top-bar nav affordance, replacing a screen title entirely
5. No bottom tab bar — a single conversation surface with history as a left slide-over panel instead of tab navigation
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Keep the canvas true black — never soften it to a dark grey; the void itself is the brand identity here.
2. Enforce strict monochrome: white/near-white text, one grey step, and exactly one reserved chroma color for links/citations — resist any urge to add a second accent for visual interest.
3. Never wrap the assistant's reply in a bubble — it is plain full-width text directly on the canvas; only the user message and any citation/source cards get a surface fill.
4. Render the streaming response as a literal teletype reveal (left-to-right, no easing bounce) with a blinking block cursor — bouncy per-character springs contradict the terminal identity.
5. Communicate elevation through surface-value steps and 1pt borders, not shadow, for everything inside the conversation; reserve real shadow for overlays that float above the whole surface.
6. Never color body text for emphasis — use a heavier weight (700) instead; color is structural (links only), never decorative.
7. Keep numerals and code set with slashed-zero enabled at all times — it reinforces the technical, machine-readable tone and should never be toggled off.
8. Skip a bottom tab bar entirely for a single-surface conversational product — route secondary navigation (history, settings) through a slide-over panel or pushed screen instead.
9. Do not ship a light mode for this specific dark-only identity — if the brief requires one, treat it as an explicit deviation and flag it rather than quietly softening the black.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in long-form reading experiences. You believe the reading surface should behave like paper, not an app screen, and you know how to make chrome disappear and reappear without ever feeling like it's fighting the reader.

<reference_data>
Color roles:
- Five reading themes, each independent of OS appearance — White (#FFFFFF page / #1A1A1A ink), Sepia default (#FBF0D9 page / #5F4B32 ink), Green (#C5E1C5 / #33492F), Dark (#2A2A2A / #D8D8D8), Black/OLED (#000000 / #C8C8C8 — dimmed ink, not pure white, to reduce halation)
- Amazon Orange #FF9900 (pressed #E88B00) — the SINGLE brand accent across the whole app: primary CTA, reading-progress fill, active-theme ring, selected tab; no second accent exists
- Chrome (Home/Library/settings, follows OS light/dark separately from the reading surface): Kindle Black #1A1A1A, Chrome Canvas #FFFFFF light / #0E0E0E dark, Surface Subtle #F4F2EE / #1A1A1A-#242424
- Link Blue #1A98FF (chrome hyperlinks), Kindle Blue #4FB3D9 (sparing accessibility/X-Ray highlight accent)

Type ladder (reading serif + UI sans, both user-adjustable in the reader):
- Reading body (Bookerly on-brand / Bitter as a free analog) at ~15.5pt/400, 1.72 line-height, justified AND hyphenated — never ragged-left by default
- Chapter title 24pt/700 serif; optional single drop-cap ~52pt/700 on a chapter's first paragraph only, never elsewhere
- Chapter eyebrow 11pt/700 tracked 1.5pt uppercase at 55% ink opacity
- UI/chrome face (Amazon Ember / SF Pro fallback): screen titles 30pt/700, book title 20pt/700, metadata 14pt/400, tab labels 10pt/500
- The reading face, size, line-spacing, and margins are always user-selectable — never hard-code one combination

Spacing/radius/shadow:
- Reading margins are user-controlled (Narrow/Standard/Wide, default ~26pt); chrome content inset 16pt; library cover gutter 14pt
- Radii: 0pt on the reading page itself (paper is square-edged), 4pt cover art, 6-8pt buttons/search fields, 12pt bottom sheets, 500pt filter pills, 50% theme swatches
- The reading page has ZERO elevation (no shadow, no border — paper doesn't shadow itself); the only shadowed objects are library cover art (a real object) and floating sheets

Named distinctive patterns:
1. Chrome-fade reading page — all navigation/status/tab chrome fades out ~250ms after a book opens; a single center-tap brings it back, edge-tap or swipe turns pages
2. The Aa typography panel — a bottom sheet with font/size/spacing/margin controls and five round theme swatches, the active one ringed in the single brand accent
3. Library cover cell — full-color 2:3 cover art with a thin brand-accent progress bar pinned to its bottom edge
4. Reader footer whisper — a muted, low-opacity percent-and-time-remaining readout plus a 2pt accent progress hairline, the only persistent reading-page UI
5. Text-selection highlight/note popover with multiple highlight-color chips plus lookup/translate/share actions
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Make the reading page itself the product — fade every piece of chrome (nav, status bar, tab bar) out on content open, and restore it only on an explicit center-tap, never leave it persistently visible while reading.
2. Default to a warm paper theme (not pure white or true black) and let the reader's own theme choice override the OS light/dark setting entirely — the reading surface and the app chrome are two independently-themed contexts.
3. Set reading body copy justified AND hyphenated at a generous line-height (~1.7) in a true reading serif — ragged-left sans body text breaks the paperback illusion this system depends on.
4. Reserve the single brand accent color for exactly four jobs — primary CTA, progress fill, active-theme-swatch ring, selected tab — and introduce no second accent anywhere in the product.
5. Never put a card, border, or shadow on the reading page itself; the only elevated objects are cover art (a physical object) and transient bottom sheets.
6. Always make reading font, size, line-spacing, and margins user-adjustable controls rather than fixed values — the whole reading layout must scale gracefully across every user setting.
7. Allow at most one ornamental drop-cap, and only on a chapter's opening paragraph — never repeat it elsewhere in the text.
8. On any true-black or near-black reading theme, dim the ink color rather than using pure white text, to reduce eye strain/halation.
9. Keep chrome-context navigation neutral and quiet (no decorative color) so it never visually competes with the reading page it leads into.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line concept:
- What long-form content is being read (books, articles, documents, scripts, etc.):
- Reading themes needed (all five, or a subset):
- Reading serif and UI sans typefaces to use (or the reference Bitter/Ember substitutes):
- Whether annotations/highlights/notes are in scope:
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version, iPad two-page-spread support):
- Existing brand accent color to substitute for Amazon Orange, if different:
- Library/catalog browsing requirements (grid, list, or both):
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` and `Font` token extension implementing all reading themes, the single-accent system, and the reading-serif/UI-sans type ladder.
2. A chrome-fading reading-page view: justified/hyphenated text rendering, chapter eyebrow/title, optional drop-cap, and the footer progress whisper.
3. An Aa-style typography bottom sheet: font/size/line-spacing/margin controls and the five-swatch theme picker with the accent-ring selection state.
4. A library cover-grid cell component with the bottom-edge progress bar and downloaded-state badge.
5. A 'continue reading' home-card component surfacing the most recent item with its progress and primary CTA.
6. A text-selection highlight/note popover component with multiple highlight-color options.
7. A short accessibility note on Dynamic Type behavior (in-app reading-size control vs. system-wide chrome scaling) and on Reduce Motion handling for chrome fades and page turns.
</what_to_give_me>
